title: One line per official
question: For every supervisor and mayor since 2015, what do the files show at a glance: money raised, who it came from, what they sponsored, and what is on record about gifts, requests, staff and enforcement?
finding: The roster holds 36 officials: 34 supervisors and 4 mayors, 2 of whom were both. Their candidate committees report $28.2 million raised from others; 4.4% of it came from organizations, or donors naming an employer, that are counterparties of a Board money file or clients of lobbyists who contacted that official. London N. Breed raised the most ($4.0 million); the highest share from such parties among those who raised $100,000 or more is 7.2% (Matt Dorsey). 13 officials appear in an Ethics Commission penalty.
how: One row per person on the roster: supervisors as the seat table in the votes analysis derives them from roll calls, mayors and one short-serving supervisor from Form 700 statements. “Raised” is itemised money received by every committee the Ethics Commission’s register ties to the person as a candidate, for any office and year on file, leaving out the candidate’s own money. “From parties” is the part given by organizations in their own name, or by donors who wrote an employer, where that organization is the named counterparty of any Board contract, grant, lease, loan or settlement file since 2014 or the client in a lobbyist’s reported contact with this official. Sponsored files and dollars, connected dollars, requested payments, gifts, excusals, staff moves and enforcement are the totals of the screens that follow; excusals are items on which the roll call prints the member “Excused” while the member voted on other items that day (land-use items, and single money-file items), plus recusal notices.
limits: Being connected is not being corrupt. The columns are not comparable across eras: sponsors of ordinary legislation are on disk only from 2019, requested-payment reports change form in 2019, the payroll names staff from fiscal 2017, and the Mayor sponsors more contract files than any supervisor. Money raised covers every office the person ran for, including school board, party committee and State seats filed in San Francisco. An employer’s name on a contribution says where the donor works, not that the employer gave. Officials who left before 2019 show fewer sponsored files because the record on disk holds only their money and land-use files. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
